title: Parentheses Generation
statement:
List every well-formed arrangement of a given number of round-bracket pairs.

Contract
- `pairs` is the number of `(` `)` pairs; it must be non-negative, otherwise throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
- Return every string of exactly `pairs` opening and `pairs` closing brackets in which each closing bracket matches an earlier opening one (no prefix has more `)` than `(`). Each string appears exactly once.
- The order of the returned strings is up to you. For `pairs == 0` the only arrangement is the empty string, so return a list holding just `""`.

Examples
- `generate(1)` returns `["()"]`.
- `generate(2)` returns `"(())"` and `"()()"`, in any order.
- `generate(3)` returns five strings: `"((()))"`, `"(()())"`, `"(())()"`, `"()(())"` and `"()()()"`, in any order.
hints: Build a string one character at a time and stop extending it as soon as it can no longer become well-formed.
Track how many opening and closing brackets have been placed. An opening bracket is allowed while fewer than `pairs` are used; a closing one only while it would not exceed the number of openings.

Append, recurse, then undo (a shared StringBuilder works). Intended complexity: the answer has the Catalan number C(n) of strings, about 4^n / n^1.5, each of length 2n, so time and space are exponential in n; the probe fixes n and measures the cost of one call, which is constant.
inputSyntax: Input: the number of pairs, from 0 to 10, for example: 3
